newsitem.title: USA: S&P analyst cites strong dlr, cuts Coke shares.
newsitem.headline: S&P analyst cites strong dlr, cuts Coke shares.

text.p: The Coca-Cola Co, which saw first-quarter revenues decline in part because of a stronger dollar, could see further foreign exchange problems ahead as U.S. rise, an equity analyst at Standard & Poor's Corp said on Monday.
Analyst Ken Shea downgraded the beverage giant from "accumulate" to "hold" and trimmed his 1997 earnings estimate to $1.55 per share from $1.65.
"I believe the stock is pretty fairly priced right now. It's a great long-term story, obviously, but it's a little richly priced in light of the strengthening dollar," he said.
